method.title: How the calculator works
method.p1: BMR (basal metabolic rate) is the energy your body uses at complete rest. The calculator uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation:
method.p2: TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) is BMR multiplied by an activity factor: 1.2 sedentary, 1.375 lightly active, 1.55 moderately active, 1.725 very active, 1.9 extra active. Imperial values are converted to kilograms and centimetres first.
method.source: Source: Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST et al. A new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure in healthy individuals. Am J Clin Nutr. 1990;51(2):241–247. The equation was derived from adults aged 19 to 78.
app.title: Use it in Calcalou
app.text: Calcalou has the same calculator built in. It saves the sedentary value as your base burn, can add it to Burned every day and counts the activity you log on top, so you see eaten against burned and what's left for today.
faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.bmr.a: BMR, or basal metabolic rate, is an estimate of the calories your body burns at complete rest to keep breathing, circulating blood and maintaining body temperature.
faq.tdee.q: What is TDEE, or maintenance calories?
faq.tdee.a: TDEE, total daily energy expenditure, adds everyday movement and exercise to your BMR. It estimates how many calories a day keep your weight about the same.
faq.formula.q: Which formula does this calculator use?
faq.formula.a: The Mifflin-St Jeor equation from 1990, multiplied by a standard activity factor from 1.2 to 1.9. The Calcalou app uses the same equation with the sedentary factor of 1.2 for its base burn.
faq.accuracy.a: It is an estimate for an average person with your age, sex, height and weight. Body composition, health conditions and medication can change your real needs. It is not medical advice: talk to a doctor or a registered dietitian before making big changes to your diet.
faq.activity.q: Which activity level should I choose?
faq.activity.a: Pick the level that matches a typical week, not your most active one. If you log workouts separately, as in Calcalou, use the sedentary value so exercise is not counted twice.
